scenes.heading: Displaying data
scenes.sub: Pick the right graph and read it like a pro
scenes.say: A good graph can tell a whole story in a few seconds. But which graph should you use, and how do you make sure it doesn't trick anyone? Let's find out.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A builder picks the right tool: a saw to cut, a hammer for nails
scenes.science: Pick the right graph: columns compare, lines show time, pies show parts
scenes.breaks: A wrong tool just fails. A wrong graph still draws a picture, but it can give the reader the wrong idea.
scenes.say: Think of a builder's toolbox. A saw is for cutting, a hammer is for nails. Graphs are tools too. Column graphs compare groups, line graphs show change over time, and pie charts show parts of a whole. The difference is, a wrong graph still draws a picture, so it can quietly mislead people.

scenes.heading: Which graph?
points: Dot plot: small sets of numbers
Pie chart: parts of a whole
scenes.say: Here's the toolbox. Column graphs compare categories. Dot plots show small sets of numbers, one dot per result. Stem-and-leaf plots show the spread and keep every value. Line graphs show change over time. And pie charts show parts of a whole.

scenes.heading: Stem-and-leaf plot
scenes.question: Ages: 12, 15, 17, 21, 23, 23, 28, 30, 34, 36, 41. How many are 30 or older?
scenes.say: Here are eleven ages, already in order. The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the ones digit. So stem one has leaves two, five and seven. Thirty or older means the stems three and four. That's three leaves plus one leaf: four people.
scenes.caption: Here are 11 ages, already in order. The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the ones digit. So stem 1 has leaves 2, 5 and 7. 30 or older means stems 3 and 4. That's 3 leaves plus 1 leaf: 4 people.

scenes.heading: Pie chart angles
scenes.say: For a pie chart, the angle of each slice is the frequency divided by the total, times three hundred and sixty degrees, because the whole circle stands for everyone.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: 30 students: football 12, netball 9, basketball 6, cricket 3. Find the angles.
scenes.say: Thirty students picked a sport. Each student is worth three hundred and sixty divided by thirty, which is twelve degrees. Football gets twelve times twelve, one hundred and forty-four degrees. Netball gets one hundred and eight. Basketball seventy-two, and cricket thirty-six. They add up to three hundred and sixty. Perfect.
scenes.caption: 30 students picked a sport. Each student is worth 360° ÷ 30 = 12°. Football gets 12 × 12° = 144°. Netball gets 108°. Basketball 72°, and cricket 36°. They add up to 360°. Perfect.

points: Columns compare, lines show time, pies show parts
Stem = tens, leaf = ones, plus a key
scenes.say: Quick recap. Columns compare, lines show time, pies show parts. Every graph needs a title, labels and an even scale starting at zero. Stem is tens, leaf is ones. And pie angles always add to three hundred and sixty degrees. Now try the practice questions!
